key_findings: Component weighting is the primary leverage point altering composite alignment score magnitude (+56.81% for equal weights, -20.97% for argument-only weights).
Threshold changes alter candidate re-classification boundaries without modifying raw embedding similarities.
SummaCConv is the main computational bottleneck (~80% of metric calculation time); disabling it yields a 79.17% overall pipeline runtime reduction (and an 86.27% metric stage speedup).
Ablated metrics log as None/ABLATED without causing schema failures or false zero-fill artifacts.
Human correlation against binary distortion target is mathematically undefined due to constant ground-truth labels across n=6 controlled perturbations.
confirmed_limitations: Small development benchmark sample size (n=6 valid perturbations from n=100 XSum documents).
Small consensus human validation sample size (n=6 consensus pairs).
Zero-variance target vector in controlled benchmark prevents binary correlation calculation.
Rule-based causal extraction primarily identifies explicit connectives and skips implicit causality.
General-purpose NLI metrics (SummaC, FactCC) exhibit low sensitivity to subtle causal phrase modifications.
future_work_proposals: Proposal A: Scale controlled benchmark generation to n=500+ validated perturbations across multi-domain datasets.
Proposal B: Fine-tune cross-encoder NLI models specifically on causal argument pair datasets.
Proposal C: Collect balanced crowd annotations including non-distorted baseline summary controls to eliminate zero-variance targets.
